package_info.package_manager: Linux distribution package managers (e.g., apt, yum, pacman)
package_info.package_versions: Affected versions as referenced in the XZ supply chain attack (e.g., 5.6.0, 5.6.1)
package_info.why_malicious: The XZ package was compromised with malicious code that targeted the SSH process, allowing attackers to bypass SSH authentication and gain unrestricted access to Linux servers. This represents a severe supply chain attack, as the malicious code was inserted upstream and distributed through official channels.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when SSHD is invoked and liblzma is loaded)
execution_context.file_location: liblzma (part of the XZ package), specifically in the build artifacts of the compromised versions

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious code embedded in liblzma that hooks into the SSHD process, intercepts authentication routines, and allows unauthorized access.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The code hooks into the SSHD authentication process by exploiting the way liblzma is loaded by SSHD. It intercepts authentication checks, allowing attackers to bypass normal authentication and gain root or privileged access to the system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: liblzma is a compression library and should not interact with authentication routines or SSHD internals. The presence of code that manipulates authentication is highly anomalous.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal liblzma code is limited to compression/decompression. It should not contain hooks or logic that interacts with SSHD or authentication mechanisms.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None. Compression libraries should not interact with authentication or process control.
key_indicators: Code that hooks or patches SSHD authentication routines
Presence of obfuscated or non-standard C code in a compression library
Behavior that enables privilege escalation or authentication bypass

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is inserted into the XZ/liblzma source code upstream.
attack_chain.leads_to: Distribution of compromised XZ package through official channels

attack_chain.action: Compromised XZ package is installed on target systems, replacing legitimate liblzma.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present on the system and loaded by processes using liblzma

attack_chain.action: When SSHD loads liblzma, the malicious code hooks into the authentication process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can bypass SSH authentication and gain unauthorized access

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits the backdoor to gain root or privileged access to the server.

behavioral_signatures: liblzma or XZ package containing code that interacts with SSHD or authentication routines
Unexpected process injection or hooking behavior from compression libraries
Obfuscated or non-standard code in open source libraries
file_indicators: liblzma.so with non-standard symbols or additional sections
XZ package versions 5.6.0, 5.6.1 (or other known compromised versions)
Unexpected changes in the build artifacts of XZ/liblzma
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections from SSHD or liblzma processes
SSH authentication logs showing successful logins without valid credentials
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installation of known compromised XZ/liblzma versions. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes in liblzma.so. Analyze the library for unexpected symbols, code sections, or authentication-related logic. Monitor SSHD logs for anomalous authentication events and investigate any unexpected network activity originating from SSHD or liblzma. Employ behavioral analysis to flag compression libraries exhibiting process injection or authentication bypass behaviors.
